guides.notes:
Review notes & scope Checked 2026-10-29

Selected profiles reviewed 2026-10-29. One released guide entry reviewed against 148 selected profiles using complete official narrative/trivia galleries, selected Databank evidence and explicitly scoped image checks. Physical scenes and transmissions are distinguished. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent. 
[1]
[131]
[2]

Lieutenant Lyste is the same officer as the existing Supply Master Lyste dossier: the official Yogar profile explicitly describes the promotion. No duplicate Yogar identity or retroactive title change is created.

Bail sends the mission, Alderaan is discussed and Ezra looks at a family photograph. These facts do not establish a living Bail/Ephraim/Mira scene or a visit to Alderaan. Leia is physically present on Lothal.

Lothal Depot is a landing area within Lothal, not another planet. The three Hammerhead hulls are marked P1–P3; a type-family connection does not identify a particular later Scarif hull or import Knights of the Old Republic specifications.

The walker’s precise model and the lieutenant’s shuttle identity remain unestablished in this selected review. No AT-DP, AT-AT or Lambda/Sentinel row is silently inferred from generic walker/shuttle wording.

Review notes & scope Checked 2026-10-29

Selected profiles reviewed 2026-10-29. One released guide entry reviewed against 148 selected profiles using complete official narrative/trivia galleries, selected Databank evidence and explicitly scoped image checks. Physical scenes and transmissions are distinguished. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent. 
[212]
[183]
[213]

The official released image 1 physically shows Ezra and Zeb alongside the named briefing participants. Rex and Sato are physically present there; Chopper is explicitly assigned to the actual mission. A Ghost crew label alone does not identify the briefing vessel as the Ghost or Liberator.

The camp is on the third moon of the Concord Dawn system. This review adds the named camp as the visited setting, without certifying the old Concord Dawn planet’s identity, world statistics or a surface visit to that planet.

The Fang fighter is explicitly the Protectors’ craft in its Databank profile and named episode clip; the guide’s related Gauntlet design is not substituted. The visiting Imperial officer and shuttle in caption 10 remain without a named identity in the selected evidence; the image does not settle that officer’s name.

Kanan recalls Mygeeto and Rau’s Clone Wars actions. Mygeeto, Rako Hardeen, Obi-Wan, Boba Fett and the naming/design references are not new episode appearances. Rau’s conditional safe passage after capture is distinct from his later voluntary rebel allegiance.

Review notes & scope Checked 2026-10-29

Selected profiles reviewed 2026-10-29. One released guide entry reviewed against 148 selected profiles using complete official narrative/trivia galleries, selected Databank evidence and explicitly scoped image checks. Physical scenes and transmissions are distinguished. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent. 
[67]
[161]
[68]
[20]

The Nixus Hub 218 name in trivia 4 is not silently equated to the existing station profile: that caption places the outpost on the same world as the earlier hub, while Brothers of the Broken Horn trivia 2 calls its hub a station. Current location/identity remains unresolved. No duplicate hub or unreviewed world is created.

Lasan is recalled and Lira San is first mapped, then actually reached: captions 24–25 establish Zeb taking Gron and Chava there and returning. Lira San/Lirasan are spelling variants of one source identity, not two worlds. Lasan is not a present-day visited setting in this review.

Hondo has actual outpost scenes and later remote conversation, so the combined row is direct. Kallus is physically shown from his own bridge in released image 22 as well as contacted remotely; direct does not place him aboard the Ghost. His later rebel defection is not projected into this chase.

Chopper’s map is explicit; Kanan and Sabine are not individually established by the selected captions/images and receive no automatic crew-based connection. Ashla is a Force term, not an Ahsoka appearance. The script-only Gron line is not added as released dialogue.

Two earlier Zeb/Ghost rows are rechecked as direct with their original row IDs and references retained; their old evidence-check dates are refreshed. Other previous episode rows and evidence remain untouched.

Review notes & scope Checked 2026-10-29

Selected profiles reviewed 2026-10-29. One released guide entry reviewed against 148 selected profiles using complete official narrative/trivia galleries, selected Databank evidence and explicitly scoped image checks. Physical scenes and transmissions are distinguished. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent. 
[204]
[174]
[205]

The Mining Guild fighters are modified yellow craft, distinct from the standard Imperial-service TIE/LN profile; no inherited speed, crew or combat statistics are transferred. The refinery is a facility on a planetoid, not a newly named entire planet.

The purrgil are actual animals and make an observed hyperspace jump. The Purrgil King label belongs to the script and does not create an individual or subspecies. Hera’s folklore about the origin of hyperspace travel is not treated as established technological history.

A Loth-cat face on Kanan’s helmet is decoration, not a live animal. Ezra’s vision through the creature’s eye does not establish a separate visited world. The named Rodian crew are supported by trivia 2; that note’s suggestion about atmosphere is not converted into a measured composition or universal species physiology.

Zeb is not individually established by the selected narrative evidence and receives no automatic crew-based appearance. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent.

Selected profiles reviewed 2026-10-29. One released guide entry reviewed against 148 selected profiles using complete official narrative/trivia galleries, selected Databank evidence and explicitly scoped image checks. Physical scenes and transmissions are distinguished. Omitted links remain unestablished, not absent. 
[49]
[152]
[50]

Sato is a holographic transmission in released image 3, not established as physically aboard the Ghost. Cham, Numa and Gobi have physical scenes as well as later conversation by comm; each has one combined direct row.

Numa is an adult resistance fighter here; her Databank’s childhood height is not applied to this appearance. Gobi is a close family friend, not a sourced biological uncle. Hera’s deceased mother is discussed, not established as a present-day living appearance.

The captured carrier is a Quasar Fire-class cruiser-carrier, distinct from the previously destroyed Phoenix Home, the Liberator and the Legends Flurry design reference. The precise later proper-name alias remains pending. The generic reinforcement shuttle is not assigned a Lambda or Sentinel identity.

The destroyed reinforcement vessel is called a light cruiser in narrative captions 24–26 and Numa’s official Rebels history; Cham’s history instead calls the reinforcement a Star Destroyer. This source discrepancy is retained. The selected row follows the released narrative plus Numa, and does not identify a named hull or verify numerical class specifications.

Ryloth is the named orbital context; this row does not assert a Ghost-crew surface landing. Boil’s name and the Tooka drawing on Numa’s clothes are references, not live appearances. The script-only ballad does not become a released performance.
